lessons.title: The tenant boundary
lessons.why: Every later object, from a dial plan to a recorder, lives in one tenant. Pairing an SBC in the wrong tenant is a different phone system.
body: A Microsoft 365 tenant holds Entra ID, the license pool, Teams policies, and the verified domains. Direct Routing will only pair an SBC FQDN that belongs to one of those verified domains. The default onmicrosoft.com domain is not eligible.

Before you discuss codecs, say which tenant you are in and whether the users are homed online. Direct Routing is not supported in Islands mode. Those two checks end more outages than a firmware upgrade.

chart.title: What must exist first
chart.note: Sequence, not a count of customers.

lessons.say: Name the tenant, the verified domain, and that onmicrosoft.com cannot be the SBC name.
lessons.fault: Pairing fails because the FQDN’s domain was never added to this tenant.
lessons.listen: The tenant is the boundary. Pair an SBC only on a verified domain, and do not use Direct Routing for Islands users.

lessons.title: Entra ID accounts voice will use
lessons.why: Licenses and policies attach to Entra objects. A queue that nobody can find in the directory cannot be licensed.
body: Humans, rooms, and resource accounts are Entra objects. Resource accounts are disabled for sign-in on purpose. They represent an auto attendant or a call queue. They are not a shared mailbox someone should open in Outlook as their daily driver.

Create the object, license it, then grant voice policy. Creating a resource account takes a Teams administrator role and the User Administrator role. Skipping the second role looks like a Teams bug and is an identity-permission miss.
lessons.say: Resource accounts do not sign in. Humans and rooms do.
lessons.fault: An admin tries to sign in as the queue and treats the blocked login as an outage.
lessons.listen: Resource accounts are Entra objects that must not sign in. License them after you create them with both admin roles.

lessons.title: Roles that can change voice
lessons.why: Global Administrator is not a voice habit. The role you use decides what an audit can prove later.
body: Teams Administrator, Teams Telephony Administrator, and Teams Communications Administrator cover different slices of calling and meetings. Support Engineer and Support Specialist are troubleshooting roles, useful for Call Analytics, and the wrong tool for building a dial plan.

Use the smallest role that can do the change. Keep named accounts. Conditional Access belongs on those admin accounts. A sticky note that holds both the SBC password and a global admin password is the incident, not the recovery.

chart.title: Privilege direction
chart.note: Narrower as you go right. Not a permission matrix export.

lessons.say: I will use a telephony or Teams admin role, not a shared global admin.
lessons.fault: Nobody can tell who changed the voice route because the account was shared.
lessons.listen: Use a named Teams or telephony admin. Keep Global Administrator off the daily voice work.

lessons.title: The admin-center map
lessons.why: Voice objects are split across the Teams admin center, the Microsoft 365 admin center, and PowerShell. Hunting in one pane wastes the outage.
body: Numbers, voice routing, attendants, and queues are Teams admin center work, with PowerShell beside them. Licenses, including the Teams Phone Resource Account license, are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Emergency addresses and network topology sit with the voice configuration, not with a random SharePoint site.
When the portal and the shell disagree, read the user with Get-CsOnlineUser. The effective policy is the one that was actually granted, including grants that came from a group.

lessons.say: Licenses in one center, voice objects in the other, effective policy from the shell.
lessons.fault: The portal toast says success and the user still has the old policy.
lessons.listen: Assign licenses in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read the effective voice policy from PowerShell before you celebrate.

lessons.title: Exchange and Cloud Voicemail
lessons.why: Voicemail is an Exchange dependency. A clean SBC trace can still mean a lost message.
body: Cloud Voicemail deposits the message in the user’s Exchange mailbox. No mailbox, no deposit. Overflow from a queue to voicemail fails the same way if the account that should receive the message has nowhere to put it.

Debug voicemail only after the call has actually reached the voicemail path. If the ladder dies at the carrier, the mailbox is innocent. If the ladder ends cleanly and the message is missing, the mailbox and the voicemail policy are the next read.
lessons.say: Cloud Voicemail needs a mailbox. The SBC cannot store the message for you.
lessons.fault: Callers finish the greeting and the user never sees a message.
lessons.listen: Teams voicemail is Cloud Voicemail into Exchange. Check the mailbox when the call itself succeeded.

lessons.title: What homed online means
lessons.why: A license on a user who is still homed on a legacy registrar will not produce Direct Routing calls.
body: Direct Routing expects the user to be homed in Microsoft 365. Islands mode is explicitly unsupported for Direct Routing. Those are registrar and coexistence facts, not SBC opinions.
Read the user before you assign a voice routing policy. If the pilot group is a mix of online users and leftover coexistence modes, you will debug one trunk twice and learn nothing.
lessons.say: Direct Routing users are homed online, and they are not in Islands mode.
lessons.fault: Half the pilot works. The other half is still in a coexistence mode the plan page excludes.
lessons.listen: Check that the user is homed online and not in Islands mode before you touch the SBC.
